title: Badge
summary: New optional `dot` prop: a 7px status dot before the label in the badge's own text colour, so the dot always matches the variant. Without `dot` the badge renders exactly as before (width, height, colours, markup). The badge grows by 15px (7px dot + 8px gap) when the dot is on.
apiNote: Additive only: `dot?: boolean` (default false). The dot is an aria-hidden span (no text, no role) and is not rendered with asChild. v1 markup parity test still passes for every variant (no dot by default).
why: A leading dot is the common status-badge treatment in Untitled UI, HeroUI Chip and Mantine Badge (leftSection); it lets a status read at a glance in dense tables without relying on the fill colour alone.

Using currentColor makes the dot follow the variant's text colour (and the disabled/outline greys) without per-variant dot tokens; contrast and the status word stay the primary signal, the dot is decorative.
Research references (HeroUI, Mantine, shadcn/ui, Untitled UI, React Aria) come from the task brief's research conclusions; they were not re-verified source by source while implementing.

scenarioLabels.all-variants-dot: All variants with the dot (before = no dot, the arg did not exist)
scenarioLabels.all-sizes-dot: Small / default / large with the dot
scenarioLabels.dot-with-icon: Dot together with a left icon

motion.after: None (static, like the rest of the badge)

states: Badge: add boolean property Dot (default off) to every Variant x Size combination that is used (Default, Primary, Outline, Disabled, Info, Active, Failed, Warning, Destructive, Secondary x sm/default/lg)
Badge / Dot = on: leading ellipse 7 x 7, fill = that variant's text colour
figmaSteps: Add a boolean property Dot to the Badge component set (default false). Existing variants are unchanged.

When Dot = true add an Ellipse layer named "Dot" as the FIRST child of the badge's auto layout, before the left icon and label: width 7, height 7 (fixed, do not resize with the badge), corner radius 9999 (circle), no stroke.

Dot fill = the badge's text colour for that variant: Default, Primary, Outline, Secondary #5E5E5E (--v2-text-secondary); Disabled #707070 (--v2-text-muted); Info #2F5398 (semantic-info-text); Active #067647 (semantic-success-text); Failed and Destructive #B42318 (semantic-error-text); Warning #B54708 (semantic-warning-text). Bind the fill to the label's colour style so they cannot drift apart.

Keep the existing badge auto layout: item spacing 8 between the dot, icon and label; padding sm 8/2, default 12/4, lg 16/6; heights 20 / 24 / 30; radius 25. The dot is vertically centred. The default Active badge goes from 61.48 to 76.48 wide (+15 = 7 + 8).
The dot is decorative: do not add it to the accessible label; the status word remains the primary signal.
notes: The dot is the same 7px at all three badge sizes, as briefed; at sm (20px high) it looks slightly heavy next to 12px text but stays legible. A 6px dot at sm is a possible refinement.
The dot uses the badge's own item gap (8px). A tighter 6px dot-to-label gap would need a -2px margin on the dot; not applied.
With asChild the badge cannot add elements to the slotted child, so dot is ignored there (documented in the prop).
Replaying the v1 badge tests on v2 fails 10 tests, all v1 utility-class assertions.

Measured: Badge width grows by exactly 15px with the dot (Active 61.48 -> 76.48, Failed 59.69 -> 74.69, sm default 54.3 -> 69.3); height, padding, gap, radius and colours are unchanged, so no other rows appear. Dot: 7 x 7, radius 9999px, background = the badge's text colour (rgb(6,118,71) on Active, rgb(180,35,24) on Failed, rgb(94,94,94) on Default).
Research references (HeroUI, Mantine, shadcn/ui, Untitled UI, React Aria) come from the task brief's research conclusions; they were not re-verified source by source while implementing.
